Answer review: lifecycle-derived custody, orphan reconciliation, real preparation binding

1. checkSlotCustodyAgreement derives expected custody from the Bash
delivery variant: open requires attached Action custody, closed
requires detached. Regression drives the real closeBashDelivery
transition (checker accepts; reclaim-failed state accepted) and a
closed-with-attached shape (rejected InvalidCustodyTransition).

2. Whole-execution reverse reconciliation: represented occupied
tokens must equal custody.occupied(), else OrphanedExecutionCustody.
Positive fixtures supply the complete slot population; negatives
cover attached and detached orphans. Neutering duplicate detection
now fails via the orphan check, showing the layers back each other.

3. checkSharedPreparation takes the live preparations: exactly one
model-preparing slot whose binding passes the real
Preparation.checkIntegrity, and Bash identity facts owned by
bash.Preparation. Regression uses a Store-backed preparation for
Attempt A against a valid slot/custody binding for B and requires
PreparationBindingMismatch; match, null/missing, and Bash identity
mismatch cases covered.

4. New RequestWriter failure test on baseline 41 beside the real
writer: 5 bytes submit (46), 7 more reserve-then-fail (53 held,
offset 5), owner release restores 41. Premature-refund mutation
fails at the outstanding assertion (expected 53, found 46). The
budget test keeps arithmetic-only scope with a pointer.

5. Teardown guards: extra reader in a nested defer scope (lenient
reader-count mutation now fails with the single intended
expectation, no secondary view-close assertion); probe
preparations cancel on error; Bash files acquired before the
execution guard; named-scratch reclamation recorded before result
assertions. Retained-removal gate still clears before retry.

6. Executable publish boundary: publishReservedOutput refuses open
producer aliases (ProducerAliasesOpen); reclaim closes aliases
then publishes through it. Order-swapped mutation fails at the
boundary. Named-scratch descriptor closure stays asserted
separately from accounting.
